findings.reason: the remedy as written removes the tick's own publication along with the re-publication that causes the cost, and the clause must be scoped to the owed-review pass's read.
findings.text: §19's deliverable says "no read inside the tick publishes the watch stream", but the tick's own `pointers = list_live(project=project)` (`reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:3339`) is exactly what publishes it (`reckon/crew/runs.py:1132`), so a worker implementing the clause literally stops the producer publishing its own stream, which is the seat's job

findings.reason: a limb with no record to read and no base comparison cannot be shown to fail, so the node's gate cannot prove it.
findings.text: §19's "three consecutive producer ticks for project reckon, each under 30 s" names no instrument to read a completed tick's duration and no negative control; the station's tick record carries a tick's start (`reckon/crew/station.py:433–438`, "the start is what makes the tick's age measurable at all"), which dates a running tick rather than giving the duration of a finished one

findings.reason: one verdict would prove neither, and the tick bound can land, and be reviewed, without the read-dedup.
findings.text: §19 bundles two independently closable deliverables: reading the pointer set once and passing it through the pass, and bounding the tick so it reaches the reload check; each has its own test and its own mechanism

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching the plan's next step from its followups would never reach §19, so the new section would sit unbuilt.
findings.text: `_document` declares §19 `implementable`, but the plan's only open followup is `f-tmref-004`, which recommends §7 (§8–§12 are named in its body as accompanying it); nothing in the followups carries §19's invocation

findings.reason: the section text and its own closing comment disagree, and the stale limb is a done-when that passes on the unfixed tree, so §18's gate proves only the reaper half.
